The following tutorials illustrate the functionality of *powfacpy*. You can use the *PowerFactory* project under [*tests\tests_input\powfacpy_tests.pfd*](../../tests/tests_input/) to run the commands in the tutorials locally. You can follow the link to *Github* on the right to download the tutorials in *.qmd* format ([*quarto*](https://quarto.org/)). If you prefer *jupyter* notebook format, you can convert them with `quarto convert <tutorial_name.qmd>` (assuming *quarto* is installed).


## Getting started
Start here with the [getting started tutorial](getting_started.qmd). This tutorial gives an overview of the interaction with the PowerFactory database using *powfacpy*. The methods introduced in this tutorial serve as a basis to do more complex things and to write more readable code using less lines of code.

## Dynamic Simulation, Plotting and Data Export
The [tutorial](dynamic_simulation_and_plotting.qmd) shows how to conveniently simulate and plot with a syntax similar to *matplotlib*. It is also depicted how to export data to *pandas* and *csv* formats and use external plotting libraries such as *matplotlib*.

## Dynamic Model Validation 
This [tutorial](dynamic_model_validation.qmd) illustartes the dynamic simulation of a unit model (e.g. a wind turbine) for test scenarios with varying grid voltage behaviour at the point of connection. Such tests are required for example if you want to debug a dynamic model and its controllers, validate a dynamic model according to a reference (e.g. another softare) or test the bahaviour for grid code requirements. 

## Dynamic Model Documentation
The [dynamic model documentation tutorial](dynamic_model_documentation.qmd) demonstrates how to generate *HTML* documentation for dynamic models in *PowerFactory*, specifically composite models (`ElmComp`) and their DSL models (`ElmDsl`). Such documentation is useful for project reports, or for sharing model details in an accessible format with collaborators who do not have access to *PowerFactory*.

## Importing Modelica Models (experimental)
The [Modelica models tutorial](modelica_models.qmd) shows how to create and compile a PowerFactory Modelica model type (`TypMdl`) from a `.mo` file or a `ModelicaModelSpec` with `powfacpy.applications.modelica`, without entering the declarations and equations through the GUI. The running example is a stepwise under-frequency / RoCoF load-shedding controller.

## Isolated Testing of Dynamic Model Blocks (DSL/Modelica)
The [dynamic model block testing tutorial](dynamic_model_block_testing.qmd) exercises a DSL block definition (`BlkDef`) or a compiled Modelica model type (`TypMdl`) in isolation, independently of any grid or network it will eventually be connected to. It shows both isolated testers: `BlockDefinitionFrameTest` / `ModelicaModelFrameTest` (model placed in the shipped `BlockDefinitionTesting` composite frame, inputs fed by an `lapprox` DSL - true ramps and arbitrary piecewise-linear profiles) and, for a Modelica model directly with no frame at all, `ModelicaModelTest` (inputs driven by parameter events - step changes only).

## Static Calculations (Load Flow etc.)
The static calculations [in this tutorial](static_calc.qmd) like *power flow* (or *load flow* as it's called in *PowerFactory*) or *short circuit analysis* are not the main focus of *powfacpy*. However, *powfacpy* provides a convenient interface to perform these calculations and to access the results.

## Study Cases
The [study cases tutorial](study_cases.qmd) illustrates how to automatically create study cases for parameter studies. 

## Parameter Studies
This [tutorial](parameter_studies.qmd) shows how to perform parameter studies in a concise and structured way and to generate targeted parameter modifications with minimal code, built on the backend-agnostic [`parstudy`](https://github.com/FraunhIEE-UniKassel-PowSysStability/parstudy) package (`powfacpy[parstudy]`) - `powfacpy.applications.parameter_studies` only adds `pf_parameter` (sweep an attribute across a list of PF objects) and `apply_gradient` (spread it unevenly across them instead). Compared to the 'Study Cases' tutorial, `parstudy` mutates the model in place and restores it after each run rather than materializing a persistent study case per combination - a better fit for large or exploratory sweeps (grids, Latin hypercube, Sobol sampling) where the sweep strategy, statistics and plots matter more than having a browsable, reusable set of PF cases.

## Dynamic Modal Analysis
The [dynamic modal analysis tutorial](dynamic_modal_analysis.qmd) covers `powfacpy.applications.dynamic_modal_analysis`: a `ModalAnalysis` wrapper around PowerFactory's modal analysis command (`ComMod`) that returns eigenvalues, damping ratios, frequencies and participation factors as a `ModalAnalysisResults`, with filtering and plotting. Eigenvalue *sweeps* - how the eigenvalues move as a parameter changes - are built on the same `parstudy.Study` mechanism as the Parameter Studies tutorial; `track_eigenvalues`/`EigenvalueSweepResults` then turn the resulting sequence into a consistently-indexed root-locus trajectory, with `Sensitivity`/`ParametricSensitivity` on top. The tutorial closes by connecting this to a time-domain simulation of the same parameter sweep, showing the two agree.

## Network Matrices and *Pandapower* Interface
This [tutorial](network_matrices_and_pandapower_interface.qmd) demonstrates how to export network matrices such as admittance or Jacobian matrix using the *Pandapower* interface as an intermediate step.

## Topology and Groupings
The [tutorial on topology and groupings](topology_and_groupings.qmd) focuses on the grouping of network elements into boundaries, zones and areas.

## The Global DIgSILENT Library
The [global DIgSILENT library tutorial](digsilent_library.qmd) shows how to navigate the built-in library by the folder names shown in the GUI (which differ from the coded names the Python API expects), using `DigsilentLibrary`.

## Dynamic Model Templates
The [dynamic model templates tutorial](template_models.qmd) covers `powfacpy.template_models`: Python interfaces to library templates that read information hidden in the controllers (e.g. the inertia of a grid-forming converter), `LibraryTemplateIndex` to detect which global-library template each controller in the active project's grid was built from, and `TemplateMatcher` which combines the two.

## Subsystems
The [Subsystems tutorial](subsystems.qmd) covers similar topics as the topology and groupings tutorial on zones, areas and boundaries. However, the *SubSystem* and *SubSystemContainer* clases of *powfacpy* go beyond the functionality and add further analysis for coherent network areas and their interactions (e.g. power exchange, connectivity, frequency stability / inertia, etc.).

## CGMES Model Exchange
In the [cgmes model exchange tutorial](cgmes_model_exchange.qmd) you can learn how to get started with the application.model_exchange tool to export, import or update grid models using CGMES.

## Database Interface
The [database interface tutorial](database_interface.qmd) illustrates the `Database` interface class of *powfacpy*, which provides methods to export and import larger chunks of data from the *PowerFactory* database (objects and their attributes, results variables, dynamic model parameters). Unlike exporting to formats such as *CGMES*, the `Database` class preserves a structure that stays close to the native *PowerFactory* database layout. 

## A Word on Performance
This [tutorial](performance.qmd) evaluates the performance characteristics of the Python API of *PowerFactory*. The *powfacpy* wrapper is benchmarked against the native API. Moreover, the performance improvements achieved through the caching mechanisms provided by *powfacpy* are demonstrated.
